nodes.name: Every 5 minutes
nodes.notes:
Polls rather than pushes. Gmail's push needs a Cloud Pub/Sub topic and a domain to verify; polling every five minutes is well inside the tolerance of a trade where lists arrive once a morning, and it has nothing to expire.

simple:false is required — the simple form drops the raw payload, and without that there are no attachments and no Message-ID.

nodes.name: Read any spreadsheets
nodes.notes:
continueOnFail is deliberate. A password-protected or corrupt workbook must not stop the email — the covering note often carries prices of its own, and an email that never arrives is invisible, while one that arrives with fewer rows is visible in the review queue.

rawData + headerRow:false gives arrays of cells including the header. The parser finds the header row by scoring it, and often it is not row 1 — one supplier opens with seven rows of trading terms.

nodes.name: Build the payload
nodes.notes: Everything n8n decides is here, in one readable place, rather than spread across a dozen nodes nobody can diff. Its job is delivery: what the message MEANS is decided on the backend.

nodes.name: POST /ingest
nodes.notes:
Retries on 5xx because the pipeline returns 500 for an unexpected failure and those are usually transient. It does NOT retry a 4xx: a malformed payload will be just as malformed the third time.

Deduplication is on the backend by message_id, so a retry that actually succeeded the first time is harmless.

nodes.name: Log the outcome
nodes.notes: The backend replies with what it did — 'processed as sell: 219 rows, 219 inserted'. Surfacing it here means a morning's execution list is readable at a glance, instead of 30 identical green ticks that say nothing about whether any stock arrived.
